Funding Opportunities
Almost all admitted doctoral students are offered financial support from the department in the form of a Teaching Assistant (TA) position or from an advisor's research grant as a Research Assistant (RA) position. In addition, ATOC encourages doctoral students to apply for fellowships and grants that fund graduate research. For example, several graduate students in our department have been awarded the NSF GRFP, the NASA FINESST, among others. Positions include a tuition remission of 9+ credit hours per semester, ~90% of health insurance costs, most student fees, and a monthly stipend. Students are responsible for paying some student fees, and the remaining costs of health insurance.
Typically, incoming PhD students are supported as a 50% (20 hours/week) Research Assistant (RA) or Teaching Assistant (TA) during the first fall (August 15-December 31) and spring (January 1-May 15) semesters. ATOC students typically will work as a 100% (40 hours/week) RA for 3 months in the summer (May 15-August 15). There is no ATOC requirement to hold a Teaching Assistant (TA) appointment. During the fall and spring semesters, students are limited to a 50% (20 hours/week) position.
Currently, the academic year 2026-2027 annual salary for ATOC students appointed as teaching assistants or research assistants is no less than $48,870 (pre-comps) to $51,450 (post-comps). This information was last updated on June 22, 2026.
The admissions committee automatically considers admitted entering students for fellowships provided by the University of Colorado at Boulder; there is no separate fellowship application for entering applicants. Fellowship recipients are selected during the admissions process in most circumstances or as soon as this information is available.
Our department's admissions decisions are made by a committee - not by a single faculty member or research advisor. We encourage prospective students to explore the ATOC website and individual faculty member’s websites to see if their research interests align. Prospective students are also encouraged to reach out to individual faculty members directly to discuss available research opportunities within their group.
Colorado Advantage Program
The Colorado Advantage Program introduces students to the outstanding science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) doctoral programs at CU Boulder. The program invites prospective applicants to CU Boulder during a weekend in the fall to learn about STEM doctoral opportunities, meet with faculty, tour research facilities and interact with current graduate students. Applicants for the program must be currently applying for admission into a STEM PhD program. You can find more information HERE.
